passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Our Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (“MD&A”) includes the following: an overview that provides a summary of our segments and highlights from fiscal 2025; a more detailed analysis of our results of operations; our capital resources and liquidity, which discusses key aspects of our statements of cash flows, changes in our balance sheets and our financial commitments; and a summary of our critical accounting estimates that involve a significant level of estimation uncertainty. Our MD&A should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and notes thereto contained herein. Our MD&A focuses on discussion of year-over-year comparisons between fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024. Discussion of fiscal 2023 results and year-over-year comparisons between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023 that are not included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal 2024. The following discussion contains forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ from those referred to herein due to a number of factors, including but not limited to risks described in Item 1A, Risk Factors, in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Overview We are one of the largest global pharmaceutical sourcing and distribution services companies, helping both healthcare providers and pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturers improve patient access to products and enhance patient care. We deliver innovative programs and services designed to increase the effectiveness and efficiency of the pharmaceutical supply chain in both human and animal health. We are organized geographically based upon the products and services we provide to our customers, and we report our results under two reportable segments: U.S. Healthcare Solutions and International Healthcare Solutions. U.S. Healthcare Solutions Segment The U.S. Healthcare Solutions reportable segment distributes a comprehensive offering of brand-name, specialty brand-name and generic pharmaceuticals, over-the-counter healthcare products, home healthcare supplies and equipment, and related services to a wide variety of healthcare providers, including acute care hospitals and health systems, independent and chain retail pharmacies, mail order pharmacies, medical clinics, long-term care and alternate site pharmacies, and other customers. The U.S. Healthcare Solutions reportable segment also provides pharmaceutical distribution (including plasma and other blood products, injectable pharmaceuticals, vaccines, and other specialty pharmaceutical products) and additional services to physicians who specialize in a variety of disease states, especially oncology and retina, and to other healthcare providers, including hospitals, specialty retinal practices, and dialysis clinics. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Investing in our securities involves risk. The following discussion describes certain risk factors that we believe could affect our business and prospects. The following risk factors should be read carefully in connection with evaluating our business and the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Any of these risk factors could lead to material adverse effects on our business, financial position, results of operations, and cash flows. Our business operations could also be affected by additional factors that are not presently known to us or that we currently consider not to be material. The reader should not consider this list to be a complete statement of all risks and uncertainties. Business and Operational Risks Our revenue, financial position, results of operations, and cash flows may suffer upon the loss, or renewal at less favorable terms, of a key customer or group purchasing organization. Walgreens and Boots together accounted for approximately 25% of our revenue in fiscal 2025 and, as of September 30, 2025, accounted for approximately 38% of our accounts receivable, net. Evernorth Health Services accounted for approximately 13% of our revenue in fiscal 2025. Our top ten customers, including governmental agencies, represented approximately 66% of revenue in fiscal 2025. We have distributor relationships with GPOs in multiple distribution segments. We may lose a key customer or GPO relationship if any existing contract with such customer or GPO expires without being extended, renewed, renegotiated or replaced or is terminated by the customer or GPO prior to expiration, to the extent such early termination is permitted by the contract. A number of our contracts with key customers or GPOs are typically subject to expiration each year, and we may lose any of these customers or GPO relationships if we are unable to extend, renew, renegotiate or replace such expired contracts. The loss of any key customer or GPO relationship could adversely affect our revenue, results of operations, and cash flows. Additionally, from time to time, key contracts may be renewed or modified prior to their expiration date in furtherance of our strategic objectives or those of our customers. If those contracts are renewed or modified at less favorable terms, they may also negatively impact our revenue, financial position, results of operations, and cash flows. The anticipated ongoing benefits of our relationship with Walgreens and Boots may not be realized. On August 28, 2025, Sycamore Partners, a private equity firm, acquired Walgreens Boots Alliance, Inc. (“WBA”). We have a distribution agreement in the U.S. pursuant to which we distribute pharmaceuticals to Walgreens pharmacies as well as a generics purchasing services arrangement under which Walgreens Boots Alliance Development GmbH (“WBAD”) provides a variety of services to us, including negotiating acquisition pricing with generic manufacturers on our behalf. Each of these agreements has a stated term that does not expire until 2029. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers debt service, with cash generation exceeding reported interest costs by a wide margin. The company's distribution model converts revenue into cash reliably, and free cash flow after capital expenditure remains substantial. This internally generated liquidity reduces reliance on external funding and supports the current debt load without strain.

Leverage sits below the sector median on both gross and net bases, and interest coverage exceeds the sector median. The company's debt-to-EBITDA ratio is moderate for a drug wholesaler, while net leverage after cash is conservative. This positions the issuer favorably relative to peers and provides headroom against the indicative downgrade threshold.

key_risks.text: Customer concentration is acute: the largest customer group represented roughly a quarter of revenue and over a third of accounts receivable, while the top ten customers accounted for about two-thirds of revenue. Loss or less favorable renewal of any key contract, particularly following the private equity acquisition of a major customer, could materially impair revenue and cash flow.

The debt structure includes a term loan maturing in the third year and a large senior note maturity in the fifth year, with the term loan representing a new borrowing. Refinancing risk is manageable given available liquidity, but the maturity profile requires active management. The undrawn revolver and commercial paper program provide backup, though commercial paper relies on revolver support.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is strong, with operating income covering cash interest paid multiple times over. The company's cash flow from operations is more than sufficient to meet interest obligations and capital expenditure, leaving ample free cash flow for debt reduction or shareholder returns. This capacity is supported by a large, liquid balance sheet and consistent operating cash generation.

Free cash flow to debt is solid, and the company holds substantial cash against its debt load. Net debt is modest relative to EBITDA, and the current ratio is slightly below one, typical for a distribution business with high receivables and payables. Overall, debt servicing capacity is robust, with no near-term liquidity concerns.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer presents a minimal indicative financial risk profile, with leverage and cash flow metrics well inside the strongest tier. Operating cash flow covers debt comfortably, and the company maintains significant cash and available credit facilities. The business is a large-scale pharmaceutical distributor with stable demand characteristics, though thin operating margins are inherent to the sector.

Forward-looking judgement: the credit profile should remain stable, supported by predictable cash generation and manageable maturities. However, customer concentration and the risk of contract renewals at less favorable terms warrant monitoring. The recent increase in debt from the term loan and acquisitions has raised leverage from prior levels, but it remains below sector median and within threshold headroom.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋債務償付，現金產生遠超報告利息成本。公司的分銷模式能可靠地將收入轉化為現金，扣除資本開支後自由現金流仍然可觀。此內部產生的流動性減低對外部資金的依賴，並在無壓力的情況下支持現有債務負擔。
槓桿率按總額及淨額基準均低於行業中位數，利息覆蓋率亦高於行業中位數。公司的債務對EBITDA比率對藥品批發商而言屬溫和，扣除現金後的淨槓桿率則保守。這使發行人相對同業處於有利位置，並提供緩衝以應對指標性下調門檻。

key_risks.text: 客戶集中度嚴峻：最大客戶群佔收入約四分之一，並佔應收賬款超過三分之一，而前十大客戶則佔收入約三分之二。任何主要合約的流失或續約條款轉差，尤其是在一名主要客戶被私募股權收購後，可能對收入及現金流造成重大損害。
債務結構包括於第三年到期的定期貸款及於第五年到期的大額優先票據，其中定期貸款為新增借款。再融資風險在可用流動性下屬可控，但到期結構需要積極管理。未提取的循環信貸及商業票據計劃提供後備，惟商業票據依賴循環信貸支持。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率強勁，營運收入覆蓋已付現金利息多倍。公司的營運現金流遠足以應付利息責任及資本開支，留下充裕的自由現金流用於減債或股東回報。此能力由龐大且具流動性的資產負債表及持續的營運現金產生所支持。
自由現金流對債務比率穩健，公司持有大量現金對應其債務負擔。淨債務相對EBITDA屬溫和，而流動比率略低於一，此為應收及應付賬款高企的分銷業務的典型情況。整體而言，債務償付能力穩健，並無短期流動性憂慮。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人呈現最低的指標性財務風險狀況，槓桿及現金流指標均遠處於最強級別之內。營運現金流輕鬆覆蓋債務，公司並維持大量現金及可用信貸額度。該業務為具穩定需求特性的大型藥品分銷商，惟薄弱的營運利潤率為行業固有特徵。
前瞻性判斷：信貸狀況應保持穩定，受可預測的現金產生及可控的到期結構所支持。然而，客戶集中度及合約以較不利條款續約的風險值得監察。近期因定期貸款及收購而增加的債務已令槓桿率較先前水平上升，但仍低於行業中位數並處於門檻緩衝之內。
